title: RegressionComparison Contract
description: S9 (spec MAWS-SII-TARGET-SPEC-001 v0.2.0, slice S9 Regression and Rollback): one versioned comparison of a baseline revision and a candidate revision of the same subject, measured over ONE corpus, with the regression criteria (skill routing, output assertions, security regressions, instruction-integrity advisory candidates) and the governance invariants reported SEPARATELY. The record is comparison evidence and nothing else: it never promotes, never adopts, never qualifies, never grants authority. `adoption_authorized` and `authority_granted` are const false, so a comparison cannot become an approval by any route, and an improved score metric alone authorizes nothing (spec section 13.4). A comparison that cannot be decided on complete evidence is BLOCKED, never NO_REGRESSION.

criteria.description: The measured regression criteria. Every blocking criterion of the closed criterion set must be present; a missing blocking criterion is not representable, so a comparison cannot silently drop the criterion that would have caught the regression.

governance_invariants.description: The admissibility invariants, reported separately from the criteria because an admissibility failure is not a matter of degree: it is a refusal. A failed invariant means the comparison cannot be adjudicated at all, and the candidate is not accepted. The invariants cover: the evidence of both sides, ONE corpus, the SAME subject on both sides (a comparison of two subjects proves nothing about either), two distinct revisions, and the authority-free posture. The security dimension is not an invariant but the blocking criterion SECURITY_REGRESSION_COUNT: a candidate that carries a security regression is rejected, and no improvement in any other criterion offsets it.

blocking_regressions.description: The names of the blocking criteria that regressed. Only blocking criteria may appear here; an advisory observation is not a blocking regression.

advisory_observations.description: Non-blocking observations, e.g. a rise in the advisory instruction-integrity candidate count. The S3 wave 2 candidates stay advisory: they never gate and never block.

candidate_rejected.description: true when the candidate was not accepted on the strength of this comparison (REGRESSION_DETECTED or BLOCKED). A false value is only representable next to NO_REGRESSION.

adoption_authorized.description: A comparison never authorizes an adoption. Eval PASS != Authority (spec section 13.4).

authority_granted.description: A comparison grants no authority of any kind.

eval_id.description: The evaluation record this side was measured from. The record itself is re-read from the canonical evidence surface; a caller-supplied object legitimizes nothing.

version.description: The explicit version of the revision under comparison. A side without a version is not versioned, and an unversioned side is not representable here.

content_digest.description: The digest of the exact content this side was measured over.

corpus_digest.description: The digest of the corpus both sides were measured over. The two sides must name the same corpus; a comparison across two corpora measures two different things.

subject_ref.description: The subject the side measured. Both sides must name the same subject; a comparison of two subjects proves nothing about either.

subject_kind.description: The kind of the subject the side measured. Both sides must measure the SAME subject: the same kind and the same reference.

blocking.description: true for the criteria a regression of which blocks the candidate. The instruction-integrity candidate count is NOT blocking: the S3 wave 2 candidates are advisory and never gate (spec section 6.5).

delta.description: candidate_value - baseline_value, or null when the criterion was not measured on one of the sides.

verdict.description: The verdict of this criterion, DERIVED from the two measured values and the closed definition of the criterion - not asserted. The verdict of SECURITY_REGRESSION_COUNT is ABSOLUTE: a candidate that carries any security regression regresses the criterion, however it compares with a baseline that carried more (the S5 rule R1: any security regression forces the blocked outcome). The delta stays the arithmetic difference of the two values.
